source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1967, p. 13 ("Rural District of Cookstown: Notice of Result of Elections 1967"); Mid-Ulster Mail, 27 May 1967, p. 8 ("Killycolpy councillor re-elected")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1967, p. 13, page image read): no nomination was received; the retiring member is entered in column 7, 'Names of Retired Members deemed to be Re-elected'

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 1 June 1967. Mullanahoe was the only contest of the sixteen seats; the other fourteen nominees were returned unopposed and Killycolpy, which received no nomination, was filled by the retiring member deemed re-elected. All sixteen divisions are recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1967, p. 13). Deemed re-elected: he failed to lodge his nomination paper (Mid-Ulster Mail, 27 May 1967, p. 8, 'is to continue as councillor for the area'). Columns 2-3 of the notice print 'Duffy, James J.' of Ballynagowan, Stewartstown; column 7 prints 'Duffy, James P.'. The Mail names him Mr. James J. Duffy. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
